prereg.split: B (Phase B caches); A is used only to calibrate the truncation regex (phrasings seen in split-A result text)
prereg.robust_z: z = (x - median) / (1.4826 * MAD) on the transformed value; if MAD == 0: (x - median) / (1.253314 * meanAD); if meanAD == 0 too, the feature is constant in that corpus and dropped. NaN values are never extreme.

transforms.log1p: log10(1 + x) for counts, character sizes, token counts and durations in seconds
transforms.logratio: log10(x) for positive ratios (x <= 0 or undefined -> NaN)

picks.rank: n_extreme desc, then sum over extreme axes of min(|z|, 20) desc, then session id (alias order for cc_local)

prereg.length_tercile: terciles of n_events within the corpus B split (cuts at the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles)
prereg.group_reporting: every attribute value with >= 5 sessions; smaller values pooled as '<small>'; rate = Wilson 95% (session is the unit)

permutation_null.rule: permute each feature's z column independently across sessions (keeps every marginal, breaks cross-feature dependence); count sessions extreme on >= 3 features

prereg.co_extremity: pairs of features: sessions extreme on both vs n_i * n_j / N under independence; listed when observed >= 5

sensitivity.within_stratum: z computed within stratum (swechat: content format; aiv_cu: stratum; cc_local: stratum; aiv_cc: month stratum; whowhen: split); strata with < 20 sessions get no within-stratum z
sensitivity.no_meanAD_features: drop features whose corpus scale fell back to meanAD, recount

prereg.truncation_regex: \.\.\. \[\d+ lines omitted\] \.\.\.|\.\.\. \[TRUNCATED\] \.\.\.|Output too large[ .(]|<persisted-output>|\(Results are truncated\.|IMPORTANT: The file content has been truncated\.|--- FILE CONTENT \(truncated\) ---|\.\.\.\d+ bytes truncated\.\.\.|\.\.\. \[\d+ characters truncated\] \.\.\.|output was truncated\. Full output saved to
prereg.truncation_rule: result has extra.truncated == true OR result text matches truncation_regex (harness phrasings only)
prereg.redaction_rule: event text, args or command contains the substring 'REDACTED' (release redaction markers, all classes)
prereg.usage_rule: ir.py USAGE DEDUPE: rows with usage_in not null, grouped by (session, api_msg_id; a null id = its own response); input/cache fields from the first row, output = max over rows. context = input + cache_read + cache_create, except aiv_cu Gemini rows where usage_in already includes cached tokens: context = input + cache_create
prereg.swechat_sessions_table: repo_id, cli_version, created month from data/swe-chat-pinned/sessions.parquet (attributes only)
prereg.private: cc_local outputs: aggregates; picks are aliased, carry numbers and enum attributes only

n_tools_distinct.definition: distinct normalized tool names among calls

top_tool_share.definition: share of calls on the most used tool

unpaired_call_frac.definition: calls whose call_id has no result in the session

orphan_result_frac.definition: results whose call_id is null or matches no call in the session

native_err_frac.definition: results with native_error true / results (POSTHOC P1)

marker_err_frac.definition: results with an ir.error_marker match / results

trunc_frac.definition: results matching the truncation rule / results

redacted_frac.definition: events matching the redaction rule / events

max_identical_call.definition: count of the most repeated (tool, args) call

consec_dup_call_frac.definition: calls identical in (tool, args) to the previous call / calls

gap_median_s.definition: median non-negative adjacent ts gap in seq order, seconds

ts_backward_frac.definition: adjacent pairs (seq order, both stamped) with ts decreasing / pairs

ts_tie_frac.definition: adjacent stamped pairs with identical ts / pairs

call_result_gap_median_s.definition: median of max(0, result ts - call ts) over paired calls, seconds

neg_call_result_frac.definition: paired calls whose result ts < call ts / paired calls

chars_per_out_token.definition: (assistant chars + thinking chars + args chars) / out_tokens_total

compactions.definition: compaction boundaries (CC compact/microcompact_boundary, Codex compacted, OpenCode compaction part)

api_errors.definition: meta subtype api_error (+ aiv_cc assistant sdk_error)

max_progress_elapsed_s.definition: max extra.elapsedTimeSeconds (or elapsedTimeMs/1000) on progress meta

synthetic_share.definition: synthetic bootstrap system events / (calls + synthetic events)

posthoc.what: native_err_frac denominator: results with native_error not null -> all results
posthoc.when: after the first features pass, before any z score or outlier count was computed
posthoc.why: descriptive check of the feature table: Claude Code writes is_error=false on only some results (e.g. cc_local B results: 25768 false, 1454 true, 9320 null), so the not-null denominator mixed tool families and gave a per-session median of 1.0 in cc_local; all-results is the uniform definition

posthoc.what: permutation null extended to tail counts (sessions with >= k extreme axes, k = 3..12) and the max
posthoc.why: observed >=3-axis counts sat at or below the >=3 null in 3 corpora while the histograms showed sessions with 10-21 extreme axes; the >=3 count alone cannot show concentration

posthoc.what: per-feature extreme counts by stratum; stratum breakdown of the top axis combos
posthoc.why: pooled outliers were dominated by minority formats/strata

posthoc.what: attribute profiles of the within-stratum outlier sets
posthoc.why: same reason as P3: separate format effects from within-format structure

posthoc.what: corpus followups: cc_local top-tool cluster and zero-thinking sessions; aiv_cu population turn-count spikes, bootstrap-only sessions, n_models >= 2 model sets; aiv_cc result rows x duration ratio; swechat repo x format and error-marker names of picks
posthoc.why: surprises seen in the first report's picks/profiles

posthoc.what: session descriptors (not z features): last event kind, ends with an unanswered call, the largest call->result gap with its tool and error-marker name, aiv_cc failed-resume result rows (num_turns 0 and duration_ms 0); flag_ends_unanswered_call and flag_failed_resume_rows added to the profiles
posthoc.when: after inspecting the IR events of swechat picks 1, 2, 8 and aiv_cc picks 2, 3
posthoc.why: pick 1/2 were a permission prompt answered by a rejection hours later; pick 8 ends on a call with no result; aiv_cc picks carry failed-resume result rows days after the run

posthoc.what: call->result gap counts in 2-second bins around 120 s and 600 s (all paired calls and shell calls), pooled per corpus with session counts
posthoc.why: 3 of 5 cc_local picks had their largest call->result gap at 600.76-600.96 s; checks whether gaps pile up at fixed harness timeouts
